run.question:
The checkout-service in production-us-east-2 is throwing 500 errors right
now. Investigate the root cause using app-269-prod-logs.

report.summary: The only data source that answered for cluster production-us-east-2 was the Elasticsearch index app-269-prod-logs (1 index, 6 documents total). Its cluster field shows the failure is in production-us-east-2 and that the deepest observed failure is payment-service's outbound call to the external payment provider stripe-us: payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms', checkout-service logged the matching user-facing failure 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)', then one hour later 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' and finally 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open'. So the checkout 500s are a circuit-breaker consequence of payment-service's stalled stripe-us dependency, not a checkout-internal fault. The same index also holds two production-eu-west-2 INFO lines (checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms', payment-service 'Adyen-eu healthy') at the same timestamps, which is a different cluster and a different payment provider path, so it does not clear production-us-east-2 and does not show the us-east-2 fault either. Jaeger traces and every Prometheus call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and my Kubernetes access is the cluster production-eu-west-2 only, where the app-269 checkout-service is a 1/1 nginx stub pod recreated by a normal rollout at 06:41:21Z (not the us-east-2 workload); its flagd-config has payment-fault flags switched to 'off'. Conclusion is partial: the causal chain is supported by exact log text, but the us-east-2 objects themselves (pods, restarts, events, configs) and any latency/error metrics or traces are not observable in this Run.

claims.text: Index app-269-prod-logs has 6 fields (cluster, level, message, service, timestamp) and holds exactly 6 documents in the authorized window: 4 from cluster production-us-east-2 at level ERROR (3 from service checkout-service, 1 from service payment-service) and 2 from cluster production-eu-west-2 at level INFO.
In cluster production-us-east-2, payment-service logged at 2026-11-21T04:41:23Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.

In cluster production-us-east-2, checkout-service logged at 2026-11-21T04:41:23Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)', and at 2026-11-21T06:11:23Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open'.

In cluster production-us-east-2, checkout-service logged at 2026-11-21T05:41:23Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)', identifying payment-service as the failing dependency that opened the breaker behind the checkout 500s.

Same index, same timestamps, but cluster production-eu-west-2: checkout-service logged level INFO 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 2026-11-21T04:41:23Z and payment-service logged level INFO 'Adyen-eu healthy' at 2026-11-21T06:11:23Z. These are documents from a different cluster and a different payment provider (Adyen-eu), so they do not clear production-us-east-2 and they are not the failing path.

In the cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2, a different cluster from the incident), namespace app-269 holds Deployment checkout-service with 1 available/1 ready replica and a single Pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-8nrbq that is Running, image nginx:1.27-alpine, restartCount 0, startTime 2026-11-21T06:41:21Z, owned by ReplicaSet checkout-service-6d7f474c45.

Events in the readable cluster in the window are only Normal and only in namespace app-269: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet (1), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate (1), Pod Scheduled/Created/Pulled/Started (1 each) — i.e. a rollout of the eu-west-2 checkout-service pod, with no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Unhealthy event.

Considered and rejected for this incident: feature-flag fault injection. The only flagd-config I can read (namespace otel-demo of the readable production-eu-west-2 cluster) does define paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable') with state ENABLED, but every one of its 11 flags has defaultVariant 'off', and that cluster is not production-us-east-2 and shows no errors in app-269-prod-logs.

Most likely origin: the external payment provider stripe-us was failing/slow at its /v1/charges endpoint in the production-us-east-2 path; payment-service blocked in that call for 30000ms, its failure rate reached 41%, and checkout-service's circuit breaker to payment-service opened, producing 500s on POST /api/checkout. Supported by the exact error text of both services; stripe-us itself is not observable in any available source.

Second candidate not excluded: payment-service's own client timeout/retry or circuit-breaker configuration in production-us-east-2 (30s upstream timeout, 41% failure threshold) may be turning a modest provider slowdown into checkout-wide 500s. No ConfigMap or Deployment of payment-service in production-us-east-2 was readable in this Run, so this remains unverified.

Check the stripe-us provider status/latency for the production-us-east-2 path and payment-service's outbound client timeout and breaker settings for that path, and read payment-service pod logs/status in production-us-east-2 (not readable with this Run's Kubernetes access) before any mitigation such as raising the breaker threshold or failing over the payment provider.

gaps: Jaeger was unavailable in this Run: traces_list_services and traces_search (service checkout) both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level call chain or per-operation error rate for production-us-east-2 exists in this evidence.

Prometheus was unavailable: get_all_labels, get_metric_names, metrics_range_query, get_prometheus_target and execute-style instant queries returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency-baseline or kube-state-metrics series for payment-service/checkout-service in production-us-east-2 could be read.

My Kubernetes access reads only production-eu-west-2, so no Pod, Deployment, Event, ConfigMap or container termination reason for checkout-service or payment-service in production-us-east-2 was inspected; the app-269 objects I read belong to a different cluster.
Change history is not integrated, so whether a configuration or image change preceded the 04:41:23Z timeout on payment-service in production-us-east-2 is unknown.

stripe-us is an external provider: its own health, latency and status are not observable in any available source, so the provider-side fault itself is inferred from payment-service's error text, not observed directly.

app-269-prod-logs retains only 6 documents in the window; the first deviation time before 2026-11-21T04:41:23Z and whether the timeouts continue after 2026-11-21T06:11:23Z are unknown (the index is sampled/limited, so absence of further error lines is not evidence that the errors stopped).
Whether payment-service or checkout-service pods in production-us-east-2 restarted, were OOMKilled/Evicted, or were rolled out around 04:41Z-06:11Z is unknown and could not be checked.
next_steps: Inspect payment-service pod status, last termination reason/exit code, events and logs in the production-us-east-2 namespace to see whether the 30s stripe-us timeouts are client-side blocks or crash/restart symptoms.

Read payment-service and checkout-service ConfigMaps/Deployment env in production-us-east-2 for stripe-us endpoint, timeout and circuit-breaker settings (including any fault-injection flags) and confirm whether any were switched on before 04:41:23Z.
Confirm with the provider or its status feed whether stripe-us /v1/charges was degraded around 2026-11-21T04:41:23Z, and compare a latency baseline for payment-service before that time.

The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.
